### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7bd05e7d0dd0bccd68fc6e9c13c1e1a6c7637d9d` — the merge of head `0262046319a13c871d5427ac8cc4181ce54a3c5e` into base `54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7bd05e7d0dd0bccd68fc6e9c13c1e1a6c7637d9d && git checkout 7bd05e7d0dd0bccd68fc6e9c13c1e1a6c7637d9d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee 0262046319a13c871d5427ac8cc4181ce54a3c5e && git checkout -B drift-repro 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee && git merge --no-ff 0262046319a13c871d5427ac8cc4181ce54a3c5e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 54ace18c669a776c7e849708039c7876ac534cee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0262046319a13c871d5427ac8cc4181ce54a3c5e`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #22125 against `main` at merge base `54ace18c6` (30 paths, +252/−115), card #22093 (body and all 7 comments), the PR body, its one bot comment, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run; the record template and the stamped-post relay were the only scripts invoked. Rendered 2026-10-07T23:40Z.

**Check-runs on the head.** First read at 2026-10-07T23:31:32Z: 46 runs, 45 completed (38 success, 7 skipped), 1 `in_progress` (a re-triggered `Check Changeset`). Re-read at 2026-10-07T23:35:34Z: 46 runs, all completed — 39 success, 7 skipped; newest run per name: 31 success, 4 skipped (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Console Pin Gate`). No failure, no neutral, nothing pending. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; no path in the file list hits the `GOVERNED_SURFACES` register, so this record is owed on the `packages/spec/src/**` non-test path limb alone.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: **unchanged**, and the PR says so correctly. Every edit is to a `.describe()` string, a refusal message string, a TSDoc or code comment, or a module-private constant. Checked one by one:

1. `manifestIdRefusal` (`manifest.zod.ts`): headline reordered to "Invalid package id 'VALUE'." with the key as a parenthetical locator in sentence 2; examples joined with " or ". Zod code stays `invalid_format` (pinned in `manifest.test.ts`); the regex `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` is untouched. **Right** — message only; the key is still named, which keeps the refusal-names-the-key contract the `POST /api/v1/packages` door depends on, and the changeset carries a matcher-migration sentence for anyone who matched the old "on KEY. Expected reverse-domain notation" wording. **Right.**
2. `MANIFEST_ID_EXAMPLES` value `['com.steedos.crm','org.apache.superset']` → `['com.acme.crm','org.example.help-desk']`. This IS a public export: `kernel/index.ts` re-exports `./manifest.zod` and the package publishes `./kernel`; it sits in `api-surface/kernel.json`. The api-surface gate records `name (kind)` rows only, so the change is invisible to it by design, and because the tuple is `as const` its literal type narrows to the new strings. In-repo readers are `manifest.zod.ts` and `manifest.test.ts` only; the existing pin that every example matches the pattern still holds. **Right at patch** — the constant's contract is "the examples the refusal shows", the changeset names the old and new values, and no consumer reads the literals — but the PR body's "no … type … change" is one notch too absolute; the literal tuple type did move. Noted, not a defect.
3. Four `filter.zod.ts` builders (`nullOrderingComparandMessage`, `listPositionFieldReferenceMessage`, `nullListComparandMemberMessage`, `blankRangeBoundMessage`): one trailing "Ruled DATE: …" sentence dropped each; rule, reason and repair sentences intact; the ADR-0049 anchor and #7596 moved into the builder comment. **Right.** The re-pointed discriminator in `filter.test.ts` (`not.toContain('A blank value is not a valid $between endpoint')`) names the real headline of `blankRangeBoundMessage` at the head, so the negative pin is non-vacuous. **Right.**
4. `view.zod.ts`: `GROUPING_FIELD_RULING`, `SUBMIT_REDIRECT_RULING`, `FORM_VIEW_FEATURES_RULING` deleted — all three were module-private `const`s (no `export`), so no public surface moves; their dates and tracker ids now live in the comments where the constants were. The seven `checkSubmitRedirectUrl` refusals, the padded grouping-field refusal and the `features.*` root refusal keep rule + reason + repair; `custom` code pinned. **Right.**
5. Describes that lost a date or an interface name only: field `required` / `multiple` (the `radio` clause folded into "any other type, `radio` included" — same refusal set as before), form-view field and section `visibleWhen`, section `collapsible` / `collapsed` (the new "so writing `collapsed: true` alone is a correct way to say collapsed by default" restates what the describe already asserts), redirect-arm `url`, page `kind` / `source` (ADR ids kept, the 2026-06-30 amendment date moved to TSDoc), action `description` (dangling dash removed), notify `template` (spec describe and the `service-automation` descriptor stay mirrored). **Right.**
6. `email-template.form.ts` Identity help and its four `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` leaves (en regenerated, zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES hand-translated; the translations read as faithful renderings). **Right.**
7. Generated `content/docs/references/**` (9 files) follow the describes byte-for-byte on the merged head; `Type Check · source gates` (`check:generated --reconcile-only`) and `Type Check · consumer gates` (`check:api-surface`) are green. **Right.**
8. Negative pins added or flipped (interface `\bI[A-Z]\w*Service\b`, ruling `\bruled\b|\bruling\b|\b20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b`, tracker `#\d{3,5}`) across `io-node-config.test.ts`, `notify-node.test.ts`, `manifest.test.ts`, `filter.test.ts`, `view-form-features-root.test.ts`, `view-submit-redirect-url.test.ts`, `action-description.test.ts` (derived with `io: 'input'`, the shape `/meta/types` serves). Each pairs with a positive pin so none can pass on an empty string. **Right.**
9. One downstream reader the PR did not list: `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` (around lines 1539 and 1541) quotes the OLD headline verbatim — "Invalid package id '' on `manifest.id`. Expected reverse-domain notation …" — as a clause's expected refusal. Its `verify` text ("the reverse-domain refusal naming manifest.id with the received ''") still holds, but the quoted sentence is now stale and a literal runner would mis-score it. Not a gate, not a governed path, not in the dispatch's file surface. **Escalated under ③.**

Refusal `code`s, exports, keys, schemas and the strict-object key sets are unchanged throughout. Console Pin Gate skipped because the `filter` job reported no console paths changed — expected: nothing exported is removed or renamed, and the dev's grep of objectui at `9990f9e` finds none of the changed strings.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22093-author-strings-internal-refs.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` (17.7.0), `@objectstack/service-automation` (17.7.0), `@objectstack/platform-objects` (17.7.0) — exactly the three published packages the diff touches (`content/docs/**` is not a package). `Check Changeset` green on the head. Patch is the right level: wording of describes and refusals, a module-private constant removal, and one public example-constant value change with no accept-set effect; the body names the manifest headline's matcher migration and the old/new example values, which is the disclosure a patch of this shape owes.

Clause-②: no — correct. No parse accepts or refuses anything it did not before, so neither `(widening)` nor `(narrowing)` applies; the PR body, the changeset body and the claim/triage all carry the same `Clause-②: no`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and open questions, each with its answer:

- `open_questions[0]` (round 0): top-level `submitBehavior` describe at `view.zod.ts` still carries "(ruled 2026-08-11)" because `gen:react-blocks` projects it into `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md` (Tier H). **Answered by the seat (6047193742, option A):** separate governed draft PR on the maintainer's approval; this PR is `Part of #22093`, the deferral comment sits beside the describe, the body names the remainder. The `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` guards are green. Verified in the diff.
- `open_questions[1]` (round 0): ruling dates removed from refusals, not only describes. **Answered by the seat (6047193742, option A):** triage 6041940817 directs rationale (interface names, dates, tracker ids) into code comments; the "ruling dates stay" wording is PR #13298's commit note, not a ruling; ADR ids stay. The PR body's lineage section now states this instead of a "reversal". Adopted as the seat's call within its tier; nothing in the inputs contradicts it.
- Round-1 report: `open_questions: []`. Deviations (worktree recreate on the existing branch; four exit-3 gate families read from CI; local spec suite narrowed to 26 files; gen ran inside the lock after the merge commit) — **accepted by the seat (6048943433)**, and each has its CI answer on the head: `check:i18n` and `check:skill-examples` run in `Type Check · consumer gates` (success), `check:type-check-debt` in `Type Check · debt ledger` (success), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` in `Build Core` (success); the full spec suite ran in `Test Core` and its six shards (all success).
- Out-of-scope findings carried by the seat as the card's second remainder (`sys_email` field help naming `IEmailService.send`, after PR #22087 settles the bundles) and as acceptance notes ("Airtable parity" wording, `@steedos/plugin-auth` TSDoc). Consistent with the diff; no action here.
- Serial notes: PRs #22094 (`manifest.zod.ts`, other region), #22103 (`field.zod.ts` / `view.zod.ts`), #22087 (translation bundles) are ordinary concurrency; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` green; the seat's read-only merge-tree against `15ec50e528` was clean.

Escalated to the seat (none blocks this verdict):

- **E1 — stale QA clause.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` quotes the pre-change package-id headline (item ① 9). One clause revision with a revision entry, either folded onto this branch before landing (non-governed path, no single-writer conflict in the open-PR scan) or carried as a card. The seat decides which.
- **E2 — hand-written docs restate the old Template help.** `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx` (around lines 171–176) still names `II18nService.getDefaultLocale()` and "(maintainer ruling, 2026-09-01)" in prose that mirrors the describe this PR rewrote. It is a reader-facing docs page, not form help or a refusal, so it is outside the card's class; flagged so the seat can decide whether docs and help should read alike. `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx` carries the same phrase and is release-owned (read-only).
